title: AI-Assisted Design-Space Analysis of High-Performance Arm Processors
problem: Modern Arm CPU design involves a large microarchitectural parameter space that is intractable to explore exhaustively. Designers need methods to identify which features most significantly impact HPC performance without naive parameter space traversal.
motivation: Understanding which microarchitectural features drive performance is critical for optimizing Arm processor design for HPC workloads.
method: A decision tree regression model is trained on over 180,000 simulated data points to predict execution cycles. The approach uses specialized search spaces and simulation frameworks tuned for real-world HPC workloads to map architectural parameters to performance outcomes.
key_novelty: Using machine learning regression models to efficiently navigate CPU design space and quantify the relative performance impact of microarchitectural features.
contributions: Decision tree regression model achieving 93.38% accuracy in predicting execution cycles
Quantitative evidence that vector length has largest performance impact (25.91%) for HPC
Identification of memory hierarchy, reorder buffer, and register file size as key performance drivers
Dataset of 180,000+ simulated configurations for CPU design-space analysis

metrics.other: vector length impact 25.91% of performance weighting
